metadata.title: Home Improvement Services Marketplace Residuality Stress Test
metadata.description: Explore how the marketplace must change when urgent homeowner demand overwhelms specialist capacity, synthetic participants attack trust, consent rules constrain contact, acquired brands carry incompatible histories, or AI discovery channels disrupt demand attribution.
metadata.naiveArchitecture: A homeowner reads advice, completes one lead form, an algorithm forwards the request to nearby professionals, credits or a campaign fund delivery, and a review closes the loop. The design assumes categories are stable, identities and intent are genuine, contact consent is reusable, professional capacity is available, every brand uses equivalent records, and search or affiliate attribution remains observable.
metadata.residualArchitecture: The changed design separates project intent, property context, contact identity, consent purpose and version, source attribution, qualification evidence, professional identity and verification, service coverage and capacity interval, match decision, lead transaction, entitlement, price decision, conversation, outcome, review provenance, claim, audit event, brand mapping, and analytical aggregate. Each consequential decision is versioned, explainable, reversible where appropriate, and recoverable by an authorized human workflow.
metadata.note: These stressors test the assumptions underneath a multi-sided lead marketplace rather than assigning forecasts. The surviving residues are explicit identity, provenance, time, policy, capacity, decision, commercial, and recovery records.

source.title: Residues: Time, Change, and Uncertainty in Software Architecture
source.author: Barry M. O'Reilly

stressors.name: A subsidy deadline, energy-price shock, or severe weather event creates urgent demand far beyond available specialist capacity
stressors.detection: Official policy and effective-date changes, category and region traffic, request-start and completion velocity, verified specialist coverage, declared crew capacity, lead acceptance, first-contact delay, price changes, complaint volume, and completed-job outcomes.
stressors.attractor: Homeowners rush to submit while specialists become selective or unavailable. A naive marketplace maximizes lead distribution, creating repeated contact, poor response, inflated acquisition cost, and low trust exactly when customers need clarity most.
stressors.businessReaction: Version the triggering guidance, show realistic availability before submission, collect urgency without promising fulfillment, refresh capacity frequently, pace campaigns, constrain allocation, explain delayed or partial matches, support waitlists and adjacent options, and measure useful contact rather than raw lead volume.
stressors.residue: Separate external trigger and guidance version, project request, urgency, geography, category, professional coverage, capacity interval, campaign budget, qualification decision, match candidate, allocation decision, lead price, expectation notice, contact outcome, and recovery case. Preserve the context that made each allocation reasonable at that time.

impacts.effect: The homeowner promise includes honest availability and recovery when urgent supply is constrained.
Adds availability signals, expectation setting, waitlist choices, and policy-version context.
Routes demand through capacity-aware pacing and explicit no-match recovery.
Versions service coverage and capacity rather than treating professional eligibility as static.
Balances relevance, capacity, fairness, and homeowner urgency with recorded explanations.
Communicates changing availability and alternatives without making fulfillment promises.
Coordinates demand pacing with professional supply, homeowner intent, operations, and data teams.
Makes capacity-aware fulfillment a more useful benchmark than annual request volume alone.

stressors.name: Synthetic requests, fabricated business identities, and generated reviews attack both sides of marketplace trust
stressors.detection: Contact verification, device and network patterns, repeated project details and media, attribution graphs, company-registry evidence, business reachability, credential changes, unusual lead purchase or response behavior, review provenance, complaint links, operator overrides, and confirmed outcomes.
stressors.attractor: Cheap generated content makes fake demand and plausible reputation evidence scale faster than manual review. Blocking every unusual participant destroys legitimate conversion, while permissive automation drains professional credits and exposes homeowners to unsafe businesses.
stressors.businessReaction: Layer contact, business, behavioral, graph, content, and outcome signals; hold high-impact decisions for trained operators; minimize exposed evidence; version rules; notify affected participants; provide claims and appeals; and learn only from adjudicated outcomes rather than raw flags.
stressors.residue: Separate claimed identity, verified identity, project content, source attribution, consent evidence, business-registry check, credential, trust signal, signal provenance, rule version, risk assessment, operator decision, match restriction, lead claim, review provenance, appeal, and final outcome. A suspicion never overwrites the underlying participant or transaction record.

impacts.effect: Professional growth depends on defensible lead quality and fair recovery from invalid demand.
Adds evidence timelines, linked-entity context, reasoned holds, and human appeal workflows.
Connects detection, containment, participant communication, adjudication, and feedback.
Combines explainable multi-signal integrity assessment with bounded automated actions.
Preserves claims, complaints, evidence, decisions, appeals, and commercial corrections.
Links reviews to interaction and outcome provenance while protecting reviewer privacy.
Owns policy and adjudication with operations, security, legal, and participant feedback.
Raises checked participation, review provenance, and recovery guarantees as trust benchmarks.

stressors.name: A regulator or court narrows acceptable consent, ranking disclosure, review, or outbound-contact practices
stressors.detection: Regulatory publications and enforcement, legal interpretation, consent and notice versions, affiliate placements, recipient counts, contact-channel use, ranking features, paid-placement treatment, review moderation, suppression and withdrawal events, data-subject requests, and customer complaints.
stressors.attractor: Previously accepted lead-sharing and ranking behavior can become indefensible while active requests, paid entitlements, partner agreements, and customer expectations still depend on it. A global shutdown protects compliance but strands valid projects and commercial obligations.
stressors.businessReaction: Map the affected purposes and records, stop only disallowed processing, issue versioned notices and choices, recalculate eligible recipients and rankings, enforce withdrawal across channels, preserve legal evidence, reconcile partner and professional charges, and provide controlled remediation queues.
stressors.residue: Separate person, business, project, source, controller and processor role, processing purpose, notice version, consent action, recipient set, disclosure event, ranking policy, paid-placement flag, review decision, suppression, withdrawal, erasure state, commercial adjustment, legal hold, and audit evidence. Each use of data resolves against the policy effective at that time.

impacts.effect: Partner value remains conditional on transparent, purpose-specific and provable lead handling.
Adds policy-aware placements, consent evidence, disclosure logs, and remediation status.
Carries consent and policy versions through acceptance, attribution, and settlement.
Evaluates consent by purpose, source, recipient treatment, version, and withdrawal state.
Enforces partner contract and purpose scope at every interface.
Coordinates partner changes with privacy, identity, commercial, and marketplace-quality owners.
Makes transparent ranking and contact handling a competitive requirement across local-service marketplaces.

stressors.name: An acquired marketplace brings conflicting taxonomies, credits, consent histories, reviews, and active leads while both brands must remain live
stressors.detection: Source-system inventories, category and geography mappings, identity collisions, active request and lead states, partner contracts, consent versions, package and credit balances, invoices, reviews and claims, API consumers, redirect traffic, event volumes, reconciliation results, support contacts, and service-level indicators.
stressors.attractor: A rapid database merge creates false identity matches, moves reviews to the wrong business, changes credit value, loses attribution, or republishes data under a purpose that was never granted. Keeping every system isolated preserves safety but prevents operating leverage and consistent quality.
stressors.businessReaction: Map semantics before records, segment migration cohorts, preserve source provenance, reconcile identity and money independently, maintain compatible contracts, dual-run critical decisions, canary customer journeys, expose exceptions to operators, support rollback, and decommission only after downstream independence is proven.
stressors.residue: Separate source brand and system, source identifier, canonical identity candidate, mapping decision, taxonomy version, consent provenance, contract, entitlement, monetary balance, request and lead lifecycle, review provenance, API contract, migration cohort, checkpoint, reconciliation, exception, rollback, redirect, and decommission evidence. Migration history remains queryable after consolidation.

impacts.effect: Operators can maintain coherent quality and service while source brands move in controlled cohorts.
Provides mapping, rehearsal, dual-run, reconciliation, exception, rollback, and decommission capabilities.
Treats semantic mapping and customer continuity as first-class outcomes, not a one-time data copy.
Owns versioned source-to-canonical mappings and cohort control across business objects.
Monitors dual-run divergence, service health, rollback readiness, and durable audit evidence.
Coordinates domain owners without taking permanent ownership of every migrated capability.
Makes portfolio integration speed and preserved marketplace trust a strategic differentiator.

stressors.name: Search and AI answer engines absorb comparison journeys and obscure the channel that created homeowner intent
stressors.detection: Organic impressions and clicks, answer-engine referrals, unattributed direct sessions, affiliate placement and click IDs, embedded-form completions, category content use, request quality, consent provenance, acquisition cost, assisted conversion, branded search, returning homeowners, and downstream matched outcomes.
stressors.attractor: Advice can be summarized without a visit while recommendation interfaces intermediate the homeowner relationship. Last-click attribution undervalues useful guidance and partners, aggressive data capture degrades trust, and optimizing only form volume produces shallow or duplicated intent.
stressors.businessReaction: Publish structured and provenance-rich guidance, make the direct product useful beyond content, accept governed partner and agent interfaces, capture declared and observed source evidence, evaluate contribution across the full request outcome, reward qualified intent, and build consented return paths independent of any single discovery channel.
stressors.residue: Separate content claim and source, content and taxonomy version, distribution channel, partner or agent identity, placement, referral evidence, declared source, session, consent action, project-intent event, request, qualification decision, match outcome, attribution model version, contribution result, settlement, and homeowner return. Re-attribution creates a new decision rather than rewriting the original trail.

impacts.effect: The direct marketplace must earn adoption through project memory, trustworthy choice, and recovery rather than content access alone.
Supports agent, embed, link, and API channels under one attribution and consent contract.
Allows a homeowner to enter with prior context while confirming the authoritative project brief and sharing choice.
Versions structured guidance, source provenance, jurisdiction, and calls to action for owned and external surfaces.
Separates source evidence from mutable attribution and settlement decisions.
Measures assisted contribution, request quality, and completed marketplace outcomes with explicit model versions.
Owns useful direct project progress while collaborating with Partner Exchange on off-platform discovery.
Makes durable direct utility and auditable contribution more important than search comparison traffic alone.

freshStressorTest.note: The naive lead-form architecture handles ordinary request forwarding but not the combined identity, policy, capacity, commercial, and provenance changes. The residual model retains independent, versioned records and controlled recovery paths for all five tests.
